## Setup

The environment is pinned in `pixi.toml`. Install [pixi](https://pixi.sh), then:

```bash
pixi install
pixi shell
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Windows

Several of these tools come from bioconda, which does not build for Windows.
Work inside **WSL2**, not native Windows.
:::

## Layer 1 — Do

Run the reference implementation on the example data and look at what comes out.

```bash
cd practicals/01-alignment
head data/sequences.fasta
```

Two sequences. Before computing anything, guess: where do you expect the gaps?
Write the guess down — you will compare against it.

## Layer 2 — Compute (start here, finish before the next session)

{{< include /shared/partials/compute-layer.qmd >}}

```bash
cd practicals/01-alignment/starter
pytest test_alignment.py -v
```

Everything fails to begin with. Work down the file; the tests are the
specification.

| | |
|---|---|
| `score` | one cell of the matrix |
| `align` | the recurrence, and the traceback |

::: {.callout-important}
## One of these has an obvious implementation that is wrong

The traceback is the one the tests are built around. Two alignments can have the
same score and different gap placement, and only one of them is what the
recurrence actually produced.
:::

## Layer 3 — Interrogate

Answer these in your write-up. They are the ones you will be asked about.

1. **Compare your alignment against Biopython's `PairwiseAligner`.** Same score?
   Same alignment? **If the scores match but the alignments differ, that is not a
   bug** — explain why.
2. **Change the gap penalty and run it again.** At what value does the alignment
   change character? What does that tell you about reporting an alignment without
   reporting its parameters?
3. **Where did your guess from Layer 1 turn out to be wrong**, and why?

::: {.callout-note}
## There is no correct setting

Only a defensible one. What is not defensible is choosing without looking.
:::

## Obstacles

Some of these you will hit. **Write them down as they happen**, not afterwards
from memory — a record of what went wrong is much harder to reconstruct at the
end of a semester than to keep as you go.

- The traceback runs off the edge of the matrix, and the error names a line that
  is not where the mistake is.
- Two alignments with the same score look like a failing test.

## What to commit

| | |
|---|---|
| `practicals/01-alignment/starter/alignment.py` | the file you filled in, tests passing |
| your write-up | the three answers above, and the obstacles you hit |

## Tools and further reading

Every tool has a manual, and every one of them was somebody's research project.
**Read the manual before you trust a default** — that habit is worth more than
anything else in this session. The paper says what the tool was built to do,
which is often narrower than what people use it for.

- **Biopython** — [docs](https://biopython.org/wiki/Documentation).
  Cock *et al.* (2009), *Bioinformatics*.
  [doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp163](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp163)
